el Raval — Barcelona, Spain

🟡 Local press research

Average day Higher caution advised night

In detail

El Raval is repeatedly described in Catalan/Spanish press as Ciutat Vella's main hotspot for drug-related crime: ARA (2024-2025, English edition) documented open-air drug dealing and consumption visible from cafe terraces, and residents told El Debate (Oct 2025) and MetropoliAbierta (Sept-Oct 2025) that 'narcopisos' (drug-dealing squats) are proliferating and that they've hired private security out of fear of robbery and occupation. A June 2026 brawl between rival groups on Rambla del Raval led to multiple arrests and prompted Mossos d'Esquadra and Guardia Urbana to install a permanent summer police post; citywide Mossos arrest data shows detentions in Ciutat Vella rising sharply since 2018. This is a mix of high property-crime exposure and real (if localized, often drug-market-linked) violence, distinct from random street muggings of tourists. Sources checked: ARA (English) - drug dens in the Raval; El Debate, Oct 2025; MetropoliAbierta, Oct 2025 / June 2026; El Caso/ElNacional, June 2024.
